name: The Phoenix Marathon
typicalWeather: Average high of about 65 °F (18 °C), with lows in the 40s °F at the start (race site)
summary: The Phoenix Marathon is held in December and is USATF certified. It starts at the base of South Mountain Park and runs north through Phoenix to a finish inside Steele Indian School Park. About 11 miles of the route are on the paved Salt River trail.
courseHighlights: Start at the South Mountain Park Visitor Center
Central Avenue north through south Phoenix
Salt River trail from about mile 5 for roughly 11 miles, out and back
Arizona State Capitol, downtown, ASU Downtown campus and Hance Park
Finish inside Steele Indian School Park

paceStrategy.summary: The race site does not list elevation numbers in its course text, so use the official profile on the course page. The route is mostly city streets and a paved river path, with one short climb onto the Hance Park deck.

segments.terrain: Quiet residential streets on Central Avenue
segments.advice: Start at goal pace or slightly slower and settle in.

segments.terrain: Paved Salt River trail, out and back
segments.advice: Hold an even pace on the open path and use other runners for shelter.

segments.terrain: Downtown streets, Capitol, ASU Downtown, short climb onto the Hance Park deck
segments.advice: Run the short climb by effort and recover on the other side.

segments.terrain: North on 3rd Street, then a loop in Steele Indian School Park
segments.advice: Hold your pace to the finish inside the park.

fuelingNotes: The race site lists about 12 aid stations on the marathon course, roughly every 2 miles. They offer Gatorade Endurance and water, and some also have Carbs Fuel energy gels. Check the aid station map on the site.
tips: All marathon runners must use the race buses to reach the South Mountain Park start; cars are not allowed through the gates
Buses leave from the Arizona State Fairgrounds parking areas, so plan your morning around them
Dress for a cool start: the race site lists a low around 42 °F (6 °C) before sunrise
The course may change, so check the course page for the latest map and GPX file

faq.question: Is the Phoenix Marathon flat?
faq.answer: The route is mostly city streets and a paved river trail. The race site does not state an elevation figure in its text, and it mentions one short climb onto the Hance Park deck.

faq.question: When is the Phoenix Marathon held?
faq.answer: It is held on a Saturday in December.

faq.question: Where does the Phoenix Marathon finish?
faq.answer: It finishes inside Steele Indian School Park in Phoenix.
